Quick diagnostic: attached pool metrics for the last hour. Early look shows an autoscale lag combined with large concurrent KV cache misses for the model shard serving FintechCo. Observations:
- GPU pool "pool-42" reached 98% utilization at ~07:30 and queue depth spiked 
- Autoscaler added nodes but the warm-up/placement delay meant load spilled into fallback causing 5xx from OOM and backend queue timeouts
- A portion of requests are arriving simultaneously due to their batch job schedule (reconciliation). Retry amplification visible in request trace ids.

Immediate mitigations I can run now (low blast):
1) Increase pool max nodes + force immediate scale action (will take ~4-6 mins to be effective)
2) Evict best-effort workloads (non-critical tenants) from pool-42 to free GPU capacity now
3) Apply short term request admission control: reduce max concurrency per connection to limit queueing
4) Temporary model downgrade for FintechCo route to a smaller quantized variant to reduce memory pressure

I'll attach pool_metrics_0601.csv with traces. If we need instant relief before nodes warm up, we should combine (2) + (3) + (4).

Attachment: pool_metrics_0601.csv

- Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Agree with Marcus. Action plan (executes in parallel):
- Priority 1 (0-10m): Evict non-prod workloads from pool-42 and drop low-priority batching jobs. Flip route weight so FintechCo gets isolated capacity.
- Priority 2 (5-15m): Apply admission control (token-bucket per-customer) at the edge; set soft 20% reduction in concurrency for FintechCo until stabilization.
- Priority 3 (5-20m): Serve FintechCo on the quantized v2 model variant (auto-fallback) to reduce memory/KV pressure. We'll mark this as temporary and monitor quality metrics.
- Priority 4 (15-60m): Force scale-up of pool-42 (warm-up) and monitor for OOM/queue events.

I will coordinate with infra to make the eviction immediate. Monica, please hold the comms draft until we confirm actions, then send a concise note to FintechCo with mitigation and ETA.

Team —

Final update for this thread: stabilization completed; root cause confirmed as autoscaler warm-up lag combined with memory pressure from large KV cache misses during FintechCo batch window. We executed eviction + admission control + temporary model downgrade; pool scaled and error rates returned to baseline in ~38 minutes.

Impact summary (customer-facing):
- Incident window: 07:30 - 08:08 PDT (approx)
- Peak 5xx/429 rate: 18% of requests for ~8 minutes
- Customers affected: FintechCo production payments route (single high-volume batch window)
- Mitigation: immediate eviction of non-prod, edge concurrency limits, routed to quantized model variant, forced scale-up of pool-42

Follow-ups / actions for leadership:
- Short term (this week): implement a fast-path warm pool mechanism for scheduled batch windows (pre-warm triggers) and reduce autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools handling scheduled jobs.
- Medium term: introduce per-customer safe-guards (batch-window detection + predictive scaling) and stricter admission-control defaults to prevent retry amplification.
- Customer ask: Monica will propose a 25% one-off credit for the incident window and offer a short technical review to adjust FintechCo's job schedule.

Aditya — please include this summary in the customer executive note and propose credits / commercial remediation. I will prepare a short internal exec brief for the Leadership team noting that this is a capacity/serving policy gap (not a model correctness issue).

Thanks all for the quick response.
